title: Records, canonical emission, validation, config, and check
summary: Record parsing, canonical JSONL emission, validation, configuration, and `check` (playbook, 'A proposed Tasks sequence', item 2). Nothing else can be proved until the port can read a store and write back the same bytes.

title: Read queries: list, show, inbox, next, agenda, projects, filters, and JSON envelopes
summary: Read-only domain behavior over an immutable snapshot (playbook item 3). Availability, lead gating, and recurrence are held back for campaign 5; every slice here says so in its oracle_gaps.

title: Mutations: basic, placement, lifecycle, projects, delegation, and proposals
summary: Playbook item 4 in full: create, changeset apply, update stamp, placement and delete on a real canonical writer, then the lifecycle half — state transitions and the DONE cascade, section and project mutation, delegation assignment and claim/release, proposal decisions, and the mutation `--json` envelopes. Seeded as one campaign because the playbook's item 4 is one item and campaign numbers are the playbook's; the second half was previously recorded only as a sentence saying it was not sliced, which `progress` could not count. Temporal verbs stay with campaign 5, revisions and the journal with campaign 6, archiving with campaign 7.

title: Temporal parsing, availability, recurrence, time zones, and calendar edges
summary: Playbook item 5, 28 slices. Everything the port needs to understand a date, a time zone, a recurrence cookie and a lead span, and then everything that WRITES one: fuzzy and expression date parsing, IANA zone resolution and the temporal context, the `{local, timezone, fold}` value type and its instants, the org-mode repeater grammar in two halves (interval cookies and calendar grammar) plus occurrence math and `explain`, the lead-span grammar and the lead availability gate, the derived availability model, the temporal `check` rules, the dated and recurrence CLI verbs, and the store-level date stamps, recurrence attach/advance, calendar roll and guard, lead write rules and skip-activation, and the atomic temporal patch changeset. Phase 3 rather than Phase 2 (corrected 2026-08-02): the campaign was labelled read-only because its front half is, but half its slices mutate and every one of those depends on campaign 4, which is Phase 3 — a campaign cannot be Phase 2 and depend on Phase 3. The plan's Phase 3 lists recurrence by name. The read-only front half (parsing, zones, availability, check, preview) is genuinely Phase 2 work and can be started against the Phase 2 gate; the phase label records where the campaign COMPLETES, not where it begins.

title: Locking, revisions, rollback, journal, undo/redo, and coalescing
summary: Playbook item 6, 11 slices: the store's advisory file lock and external-change detection, the three-component revision token and the two staleness surfaces built on it, the checked write with its post-write validation and rollback, the on-disk journal (directory identity, index, content-addressed blobs, cap and garbage collection) and its containment contract against a corrupt or hostile journal state, undo/redo apply and its failure paths, history coalescing, and the `undo`/`redo` CLI surface. Phase 4 rather than the Phase 3 string this record used to carry, which was copied verbatim from campaign 7 (corrected 2026-08-02): the plan's Phase 4 is 'port journal and merge behavior' and names 'implement undo/redo and coalescing' explicitly, which is this campaign's centre of gravity and the reason it exists as a separate item. The qualification is real and is why the choice was close: the plan's Phase 3 lists locking, rollback and revisions — `store-file-lock`, `store-checked-write-rollback`, `store-revision-token` and the two `revision-staleness-*` slices — among mutations and transaction safety. Those five are Phase 3 work sliced here rather than in campaign 4, because each of them is a rule the journal slices cannot be characterized without, and splitting them across two campaigns would have put one half of every transaction property in a different epic. They are startable at the Phase 3 gate; the six journal, undo/redo and coalescing slices are what makes the campaign Phase 4.

title: Archive and Git merge behavior
summary: Playbook item 7. The archive sweep and its two-file transaction, section archiving, the `tasks archive` surface, and the record-aware three-way merge git invokes as a merge driver. Sequenced after campaign 4 because every slice here either moves records the mutation slices wrote or merges two histories of them. Recurrence-aware selection stays with campaign 5 and the journal half of undo stays with campaign 6; both are named in the slices' oracle_gaps rather than assumed.

title: OpenAPI server, ETags, error handling, events, and cross-process concurrency
plan_phase: Phase 5 (replace the CLI and HTTP adapters)
summary: Playbook item 9, 22 slices: the HTTP adapter in full. The published OpenAPI 3.1 contract and its agreement with the routing table, the transport envelope (status codes, error bodies, content negotiation, origin refusal), service metadata and the deliberately unrouted endpoints, the per-request read model and store revision, the task representation and its collection queries, ETag preconditions, the task write lifecycle, ordered placement, proposal decisions, temporal and recurrence/lead field adapters, delegation actions, recurrence explain, the four project surfaces (reads, create, rename-and-complete, archive), the `bin/tasks-api` entrypoint, and two cross-process slices in which a spawned server and a CLI process write and read the same store. Sequenced at Phase 5 with the CLI because both are adapters over domain behavior campaigns 2-7 must already have proved. The campaign's standing methodological problem is that the conformance runner drives `surface: "cli"` only: the case list and `observations.schema.json` both carry the HTTP shape (a `surface` enum and a top-level `http` request/response array added expressly for this), but no runner emits them yet, so every slice here records what it cannot observe rather than wiring a near-miss fixture. The two cross-process slices are the exception and now carry a real `fixtures_todo`, because their oracle already drives argv at a store on disk.

title: Agent execution: harness protocol, provider registry, system context, and `tasks -p`
plan_phase: Phase 5 (replace the CLI and HTTP adapters)
summary: Playbook item 10. The layer that hands a natural-language request to an autonomous coding harness and gets out of the way: the provider/model registry resolved from config, the spawn-and-cancel contract every backend implements, the three built-in adapters' invocation shapes, the system context assembled from TASK_AGENT.md plus prompt facts plus the user-approved agent-memory.md sidecar, the `tasks -p` command, the post-run git diff, and the serial request queue. Seeded 2026-08-01 after Marcus decided agent execution is in the port (td-7fce3d), which the previous slicing pass had deferred pending exactly that decision. This is the first campaign whose behavior INVOKES EXTERNAL PROCESSES, and it is the first whose slices are largely not drivable by the conformance runner as the protocol stands: porting/specs/observations.schema.json records files, stdout/stderr and exit status and nothing about a spawned child, so most slices here carry an explicit oracle_gap saying what is unobservable and a fixtures_todo describing the fake-harness corpus that would make the observable part observable. TUI presentation of agent activity stays with campaign 12 and is named test-by-test in agent-request-queue's oracle_gaps rather than assumed.

title: Bubble Tea TUI behavior
summary: Playbook item 12, 30 slices: the TUI rebuilt on Bubble Tea, sliced in three groups that were seeded in parallel and merged on 2026-08-02. The shell and interaction group — process bootstrap and geometry, the UI mode machine and session file, input decoding and shortcuts, selection/navigation/mouse, filters and palettes, the quick actions, delegation keys, editor and project/archive integrations, the agent prompt and queue, export and clipboard, and the TUI half of config. The rendering group — text metrics, theme and border, screen layout, frame composition, view row projection and decoration, the hit map, mouse input, agent activity, and the paint cache. The forms group — the TermForm engine and its text and choice/date fields, the form surface, the choice picker and palettes, the modal overlay, the task-detail content builder, and the editor session that writes. Phase 7, last of the port, and the campaign with the most method risk: `observations.schema.json` has no frame, cell, cursor or attribute field, so this campaign is proved by TRANSLATED UNIT TESTS rather than by differential conformance — a decision Marcus took at seeding, recorded on every slice, and the reason no slice here carries a fixture or a fixtures_todo.
